reasons: Deviation classification is correct: the fifteen-day Deliverable conformity window in Section 19.2, coupled with 'Vendor has no correction or refund obligation' after that date, falls below the playbook fallback (30 days services / 90 days software) and cuts off both the open-ended Section 19.1 warranty and the Section 19.4 remedy for Deliverables, so the clause does not meet even the fallback on a material term.

The redline is valid and minimal in substance: it extends the period to ninety days (consistent with the preferred 90-day deliverables position), deletes only the offending 'no correction or refund obligation' cut-off, and adds a single non-limitation sentence preserving Sections 19.1 and 19.4. No other clause is rewritten.

The failed deterministic check on 'warranty period ≥ 90 days' is a phrasing artifact — the redline spells out 'ninety days' rather than using digits — and the 0.505 changed-character ratio is justified because the sentence's operative period and its remedy carve-out both had to change.

The comment is accurate, correctly scoped to duration and the remedy cut-off, cites the playbook minimum, and does not re-flag terms already compliant (19.1, 19.3, 19.4, 19.5 acknowledged as adequate in the rationale).
